.. py:class:: RoboTwinEnvStepReturn

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvStepReturn`\ [\ :py:obj:`dict`\ [\ :py:obj:`str`\ , :py:obj:`Any`\ ]\ :py:obj:`| None`\ , :py:obj:`bool`\ ]


   The return type of the `step` function in the environment.

   This class extends gymnasium's Env step return type to be a dataclass
   with generic types for observations and rewards.


   Template Args:
       ObsType: The type of the observations returned by the environment.
       RewardsType: The type of the rewards returned by the environment.



   .. py:attribute:: observations
      :type:  dict[str, Any] | None

      The observations returned by the environment after taking a step.


   .. py:attribute:: terminated
      :type:  bool

      Whether the environment has reached a terminal state.

      Usually the environment is considered to be in a terminal state
      when the agent has reached the goal or failed to reach the goal.

      User should call `reset` function to reset the environment
      after the environment has reached a terminal state.


   .. py:attribute:: rewards
      :type:  bool

      The rewards is a boolean indicating whether the task was successful.


   .. py:attribute:: truncated
      :type:  bool

      Whether the episode was truncated due to reaching the step limit.


.. py:class:: RoboTwinEnv(cfg: RoboTwinEnvCfg)

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvBase`\ [\ :py:obj:`dict`\ [\ :py:obj:`str`\ , :py:obj:`Any`\ ]\ :py:obj:`| None`\ , :py:obj:`bool`\ ]


   RoboTwin environment.

   This class provides RoboTwin environment with robo_orchard_core interface.
   To make it work, you need to install RoboTwin and set the `RoboTwin_PATH`
   environment variable to the path of the RoboTwin package.


   After initialization, you need to call `reset()` to create the environment.



   .. py:attribute:: cfg


   .. py:property:: current_seed
      :type: int


      The current seed of the environment.


   .. py:property:: instructions
      :type: dict | None | str


      The instructions for the environment.

      This property is only valid if the environment is initialized
      with `check_expert=True` or `check_task_init=True`.

      If in eval_mode, return the instruction from the task, usually
      a string, otherwise the returned instruction is a dictionary
      containing multiple instructions, with maximum number specified
      by `max_instruction_num`.


   .. py:method:: step(action: list[float] | numpy.ndarray) -> RoboTwinEnvStepReturn

      Take a step in the environment.

      :param action: The action to take in the
                     environment. Actually it is the joint positions of the
                     robot. The action should be 1-D array with length matching
                     the task.
      :type action: list[float] | np.ndarray

      :returns:

                The observation and environment
                    state after taking the action, or None if the episode
                    has ended.
      :rtype: RoboTwinEnvStepReturn | None



   .. py:method:: reset(env_ids: Sequence[int] | None = None, seed: int | None = None, clear_cache: bool = False) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, dict]

      Reset the environment.

      If the environment has not been reset before, or the seed is
      different from the previous one, the environment will be re-created
      and check the seed.

      .. warning::

         RoboTwin does not use local RandomGenerator, when the environment
         is re-created, the seed will be set to the one in the config
         for both numpy and torch. This may affect the randomness of other
         parts of the code!
         This is a BUG in RoboTwin!



   .. py:method:: close(clear_cache: bool = True)

      Close the environment.



   .. py:property:: num_envs
      :type: int


      The number of instances of the environment that are running.

      For example, if the environment is a single instance, then this
      should return 1. This is the case for most classical environments.

      In the case of reforcement learning, usually a vectorized environment
      is used to run multiple instances of the environment in parallel to
      speed up the training process. In this case, this function should
      return the number of instances of the environment that are running.

      The number of instances of the environment is used in other parts of
      the code to manage the environment.


   .. py:property:: action_space
      :type: gymnasium.Space


      The action space of the environment.

      Actually RoboTwin does not implement the action space!
      Call this method will raise an error!

      :returns: The action space of the environment.
      :rtype: gym.Space


   .. py:property:: observation_space
      :type: gymnasium.Space


      The observation space of the environment.

      Actually RoboTwin does not implement the observation space!
      Call this method will raise an error!

      :returns: The observation space of the environment.
      :rtype: gym.Space


   .. py:method:: unwrapped_env() -> envs._base_task.Base_Task

      Get the original RoboTwin environment.



.. py:class:: RoboTwinEnvCfg

   Bases: :py:obj:`robo_orchard_core.envs.env_base.EnvBaseCfg`\ [\ :py:obj:`RoboTwinEnv`\ ]


   Configuration for the RoboTwin environment.


   .. py:attribute:: class_type
      :type:  type[RoboTwinEnv]


   .. py:attribute:: task_name
      :type:  str

      The name of the task to run, e.g., 'place_object_scale'.


   .. py:attribute:: seed
      :type:  int
      :value: 0


      The random seed for the environment.

      If eval_mode is True, the seed will be changed in `__post_init__` to
      `100000 * (1 + seed)` to match the implementation in RoboTwin.


   .. py:attribute:: episode_id
      :type:  int
      :value: 0


      The episode ID for the environment, used for logging and tracking.


   .. py:attribute:: check_expert
      :type:  bool
      :value: False


      Whether to check the expert trajectory for the task.

      If true, the environment will attempt to run the task with given seed
      to check if the task can be completed successfully using the expert
      trajectory. If fails, new seed will be generated and used.

      This field is used to make sure that the environment can be recorded
      successfully using the expert trajectory for imitation learning.


   .. py:attribute:: check_task_init
      :type:  bool
      :value: True


      Whether to check the task initialization.

      If true, the environment will call `play_once()` to execute the task
      with expert trajectory to check if the task can be initialized
      successfully.

      This field should be set to True because some task attributes that
      required for interaction may be initialized in the `play_once()` method,
      such as `place_object_scale` task.

      This should be a BUG in RoboTwin and will significantly affect the
      performance of the environment initialization.


   .. py:attribute:: eval_mode
      :type:  bool
      :value: False


      Whether for evaluation.

      If true, the environment will use unseen texture_type.


   .. py:attribute:: max_instruction_num
      :type:  int
      :value: 10


      The maximum number of instructions to generate for the env.


   .. py:attribute:: format_datatypes
      :type:  bool
      :value: False


      whether to format obs as robo_orchard datatypes.

      If true, the observation will be formatted as:
          - "joints": dict of joint name to joint position. This key will
              replace the original "joint_action" key.
          - "cameras": dict of camera name to camera image. This key will
              replace the original "observation" key.
          - other keys in the original observation will be kept.


   .. py:property:: task_config_path
      :type: str


      Path to the task configuration file.


   .. py:property:: embodiment_config_path
      :type: str


      Path to the embodiment configuration file.


   .. py:property:: camera_config_path
      :type: str


      Path to the camera configuration file.


   .. py:method:: get_task_config() -> dict[str, Any]

      Get the configuration for the task.
